objections.objection: CE-Replay is only a handwritten PostgreSQL estimator reimplementation.
objections.answer: The bounded implementation is manual, but the representation contract specializes workload-fixed context while retaining design-parametric state transitions and their objective/dependency interfaces across hypothetical states.
objections.boundary: No automatic extraction or full PostgreSQL CE claim.

objections.objection: CE-Replay is only INUM/C-PQO applied to statistics.
objections.answer: INUM/C-PQO establish reusable plan/cost representations; the estimator computation represented here exposes internal statistics-semantic state and dependencies needed for CE evaluation and safe design-move invalidation.
objections.boundary: No priority claim or assertion that prior systems are black boxes or cannot expose dependencies.

objections.objection: q-error has no demonstrated runtime implication.
objections.answer: Correct: q-error directly evaluates the represented CE/information-state layer and is not presented as a runtime surrogate; plan/runtime objectives require effects outside this representation.

objections.objection: Candidate-payload acquisition is outside the solved system.
objections.answer: The system assumes an offline frozen payload repository; acquisition remains external and future systems work.

objections.objection: Incremental semantic evaluation can be slower in wall-clock.
objections.answer: The mixed evaluator reduces semantic-control work but is 3.23x slower because numerical aggregation and implementation overhead dominate.
objections.boundary: Contribution concerns exact invalidation/evaluation structure, not guaranteed acceleration.

objections.objection: Fresh payload drift can exceed small optimization refinements.
objections.answer: Same-realization replay fidelity and frozen-to-fresh drift are reported separately; the optimizer is not realization-robust.
The model is explicitly a first-order environment-specific proxy, not a universal or per-candidate PostgreSQL cost.

objections.objection: Two workloads do not establish universal generality.
objections.answer: Census and DMV provide complementary sparse/dense evidence but do not establish universal workload generality.
The claim is scoped to the supported PostgreSQL semantics and two frozen workload realizations, not stated as a universal theorem.

objections.objection: DMV zero-truth queries dominate raw aggregate loss.
objections.location: Section 7, Table 3 caption and [ZT] cell, Sections 8.2 and 9.7
objections.answer: The exact preserved raw value remains visible and immediately marked as dominated by two zero-truth queries; optimization still used it and nonzero-truth loss remains diagnostic only.
objections.boundary: No objective replacement, query exclusion, or cross-workload raw-loss comparison.

objections.objection: DMV paired frozen/fresh provenance is incomplete.
objections.answer: The provenance gap prevents paired DMV drift reconstruction but does not invalidate fresh same-realization fidelity or physical composition evidence.
Termination is a complete audited ADD/DROP/SWAP neighborhood local optimum; exact global agreement is limited to stated small/restricted instances.
